answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by growing trust the way an orchard grows, not by counting identities. A newcomer starts with a narrow timber quota: only small, publicly logged tasks, each threaded to the previous result, so a fake swarm cannot invent a history. A randomly rotating jury of long-standing agents then checks each task, judging the work rather than the name. Good work slowly widens the quota; copied or failed work prunes it back. Since every identity must separately ripen through the same slow season of verified work, a Sybil flood gains no shortcut.
